clue.text: It's routine to make a pudding

definitions.note: read as 'what you use to make a pudding'

blocks.note: first meaning: the basic everyday work that pays the bills
second meaning: the two staples layered with custard in a classic British baked dessert

explanation.surface: Someone who bakes the same dessert so often that it has become a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread and butter pudding is a traditional British dessert of buttered bread slices baked in egg custard.
explanation.definitionFit: Your bread-and-butter work is the steady, ordinary core of a job; literally the ingredients are slices of loaf spread with dairy fat.

clue.text: Is very fed up at being so battered or deformed

indicators.note: something deformed has been bent out of its proper shape, so the letters lose their original order

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up at having been beaten and left misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'deformed' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bored to tears is an idiom for extreme weariness and boredom, the state of someone thoroughly fed up.

clue.text: Gives out due to changing times

indicators.note: changing the word's form means its letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something breaks down or runs out because the era has moved on.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as a lamp sends out light or a chimney releases smoke.

clue.text: Conversation's sure to get animated after the dance

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving about, so the letters jump into a new order
after tells us the rearranged word comes behind the other piece

blocks.note: a disco is a dance party with recorded pop music
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chat is bound to liven up once the dancing is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is a formal word for talk or spoken exchange between people, a synonym for conversation.

clue.text: They're known for being stingy

blocks.note: surface reading: some people with a reputation for meanness with money
setter's reading: able to sting, like a common weed whose leaves leave a burning rash

explanation.surface: A group of people famous for being tight-fisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingy normally means mean with money; here it is read as 'having stings'.
explanation.definitionFit: The common stinging weeds have hairy leaves that inject an irritant, so they are famous for stinging anyone who brushes against them.

clue.text: Coal burner produced following bizarre mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up is a muddle, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange muddle somehow ends with a coal fire being made.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal basket or stand holding burning fuel, used outdoors for warmth by workers or pickets.

clue.text: A good mixer will cheer people up

definitions.note: read as 'something that will cheer people up'

blocks.note: first meaning: the fizzy quinine drink poured with gin
second meaning: a pick-me-up that restores spirits

explanation.surface: Someone sociable at a party is bound to lift everyone's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'good mixer' looks like a sociable person; here it is a drink added to spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a classic drink mixer, and a tonic is also anything that invigorates or restores someone's mood.

clue.text: Always enter new arrangement with a friend

indicators.note: a new arrangement puts the letters into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep forming new partnerships with a companion forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for all time without end, the same sense as always or forever.

clue.text: Complains bitterly in bars

blocks.note: first meaning: protests angrily
second meaning: horizontal rods, as on a fence or a track

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling sourly while drinking in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, but it means rods or railings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest vehemently, and rails are long straight rods forming fences or tracks.

clue.text: Plaything for school group

blocks.note: to school someone is to train or coach them
a set is a group, especially a class sorted by ability in a British school

explanation.surface: A toy bought for a whole class of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School group' looks like one phrase, but school is a verb here, followed by a separate noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy railway with model locomotives and track is a classic children's toy.

clue.text: The right outfit to wear to the match?

definitions.text: The right outfit to wear to the match?

blocks.clueFragment: The right outfit to wear to the match?
blocks.note: surface reading: suitable clothes for watching a football game
setter's reading: a match is a marriage, so the outfit is the bride's gown

explanation.surface: Choosing what to wear to a big sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests sport, but it also means a marriage, as in 'a good match'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride wears a special white gown for her marriage ceremony, the perfect outfit for that kind of match.

clue.text: Rob to go off following return of Edward

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the name is written backwards
following puts the first piece behind the second in the answer

blocks.note: Ed is the short form of Edward
food that goes off spoils or turns bad

explanation.surface: A robbery that turns sour after Edward comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or strip of possessions by force, the same as robbing.

clue.text: Smoker in church will cause anger

definitions.note: the aromatic burnt in a church

blocks.note: first meaning: the fragrant resin burnt in a censer during services
second meaning: to infuriate, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: Anyone lighting a cigarette during a church service is bound to annoy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette; it is the thing that gives off smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is fragrant gum burnt during worship, and the verb incense means to make furious.

clue.text: The splits - or the alternative

indicators.note: a word that splits another breaks into it and sits in the middle

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gymnastic move, the splits, or else something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The splits' looks like the gymnastic stretch; 'The' is the word that splits 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: The other is the second of two options, the remaining choice, just as 'the alternative' is.

clue.text: Designed for the baby-sitter?

blocks.note: surface reading: something made for the person minding a child
setter's reading: the baby who sits, as at a feeding table

explanation.surface: An item made specially for a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: A baby-sitter normally minds a child; here it is the infant doing the sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat with a tray lets a toddler sit at table height for meals, built specifically for a baby.

clue.text: The way badly-dressed student found inside, then wandered erratically

indicators.note: something found inside lies within another word

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
wearing torn, worn-out clothes
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A scruffy student turns up on the road and then roams aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To straggle is to stray or trail behind in a disorderly, scattered way rather than keeping to a line.

clue.text: It shows time is precious

blocks.note: surface reading: a proverb-like statement that one should not waste time
setter's reading: made of a precious metal and literally showing the hour

explanation.surface: A saying that every minute counts.
explanation.walkthrough: Traditionally such a timepiece is given to an employee on retirement after long service.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece cased in the yellow precious metal tells the hour and is itself valuable.

clue.text: It whips up urge he has to raise his game

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

blocks.clueFragment: he has to raise his game
blocks.note: on a shoot, a beater drives the birds up into the air for the guns

explanation.surface: A spur that makes a sportsman lift his performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise his game' sounds like improving performance; here game means birds flushed out on a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen whisk with rotating blades is used to whip cream or eggs into a froth.

clue.text: Foreign artiste is more piquant

indicators.note: foreign means strange or not native, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer from abroad has a spicier act.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquant means pleasantly sharp in flavour, so something more piquant has more flavour and is better to the palate.

clue.text: Audience numbers made up by sailors

blocks.note: first meaning: the viewing figures for a television show
second meaning: ordinary seamen in the navy, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A crowd mostly made of seamen on shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy, ratings are non-commissioned sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing figures for broadcasts are called ratings, and naval enlisted seamen are also known by that name.

clue.text: Provide non-professional with no backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: lay people are those outside a profession, amateurs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Supplying an amateur who has no support from anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay on a meal or a bus is an idiom for arranging or supplying it.

clue.text: Pulls back, moving closer when I get in

indicators.note: moving the letters about changes their order
to get in is to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs away as the speaker approaches and climbs aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring or shrink backwards, as from shock or as a gun jerks after firing.

clue.text: I do get confused when I'm about to give certain type of speech

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into a different order
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker gets flustered as they are about to deliver a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' suggests wedding vows, but it is just the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of expression peculiar to a language or group, a particular manner of speaking.

clue.text: Wrote strangely to editor, having attained a lofty position

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A writer sent an odd letter to the editor after rising to high office.
explanation.definitionFit: To tower is to rise high above surroundings, so something that towered stood at a great height.

clue.text: Proportion of fighting force turning up in South American city

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, usually called simply Rio

explanation.surface: A share of an army showing up in a Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is what a proportion is.

clue.text: A capital citizen?

blocks.note: surface reading: an excellent, upstanding member of society
setter's reading: someone who lives in a capital city, one in particular

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine, upright member of the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' in old British slang means excellent; here it means a capital city, and the answer is just one of many.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of the French capital lives in a capital city, so is a citizen of it.

clue.text: Name the French applied to bird

indicators.note: applied to means stuck on after, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird, such as the blue tit
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French name given to a species of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or song, or a word designating rank, so it serves as a name.

clue.text: Where one first learns the chief disciplines

blocks.note: primary means main or principal
to school is to train or discipline

explanation.surface: The first place a pupil learns the main subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disciplines' looks like a noun for academic subjects, but it is a verb meaning trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Young children start their education at these institutions, typically between ages five and eleven in Britain.
